Enterprise Trust & Safety Operations Analytics

An enterprise-style analytics solution built from an operations-first perspective: translating floor realities, KPI definitions and business rules into a governed SQL + Power BI reporting layer.

I bridge operational leadership and analytics — applying enterprise BA and UAT discipline to make data useful, testable and floor-ready.
View GitHub RepositoryView Case Study PDF

The operational problem I was solving

Trust & Safety operations can make the wrong decision very quickly when the reporting layer is wrong. The objective was not simply to build dashboards; it was to make workload, service risk and workforce signals operationally trustworthy before they drive decisions.

01 · CAPACITY

Expose hidden capacity leaks

Scheduled vs. logged hours, absenteeism, shrinkage and staffing gaps make workforce loss visible before it becomes a service-level problem.

02 · PERFORMANCE

Kill the enterprise-average fallacy

An enterprise SLA can conceal a failing site. The model supports site-level drill-down so accountability follows the work to where it actually happens.

03 · PLANNING

Move from reactive to proactive

Historical workload is converted into a 3-month demand baseline, giving workforce planning a forward-looking signal rather than waiting for volume pressure to arrive.

THE BRIDGE

Operations knowledge + analytical execution

I understand why AHT, SLA, productivity, staffing and shrinkage matter on the floor — and I can translate those definitions into SQL reporting logic, validation rules, DAX measures and decision-ready Power BI views.

OPERATIONS-FIRST DATA QUALITY

Missing data is not automatically zero

The Cebu workforce gap is a deliberate example: employees exist in the employee dimension, but no workforce activity records exist. The reporting layer preserves that distinction instead of manufacturing zero capacity.

Important implementation detail: The reporting view exposes the pre-calculated FO.SLA_Compliance_Pct; it does not hard-code a cancelled-case filter. UAT built around operational edge cases

The UAT approach was designed around business consequences, not only whether a query returned rows.

EDGE CASE · SLA

Cancelled cases must not distort SLA

If cancelled cases enter the denominator, reported SLA can be artificially depressed. The business rule explicitly excludes them from SLA measurement.

Control: KPI definition + RTM traceability + SQL-to-Power BI reconciliation target of 0% variance.

EDGE CASE · BACKLOG / AHT

Do not contaminate operational metrics

Open Backlog is restricted to Active and Pending cases, while Average Handle Time excludes system idle time. These rules prevent operationally irrelevant states from changing management decisions.

Defect mechanism: validation discrepancies are investigated against the business rule and reporting layer, then fed back through the RTM/UAT process.

Key analytical findings

Stable enterprise demand

Historical daily case volumes are highly stable, with limited enterprise-level seasonality.

Site-level variation

Average daily workload differs materially by site, making site-level planning more useful than a single enterprise average.

Workforce gaps

Required versus actual staffing highlights locations where workforce planning needs attention.

Cebu coverage gap

Cebu exists in the employee dimension but lacks corresponding workforce activity records; missing activity is not treated as zero capacity.

Data quality

Validation covered grain, relationships, dates, site coverage, KPI calculations, percentage scaling, views and forecast suitability.

Governed scope

Deferred Finance, Quality and Appeals areas remain documented rather than represented as implemented capabilities.
